_note: One row per detector. sensitivity = P(fires | front), falsePositive = P(fires | genuine): EXPERT PRIORS (est.) until learned from labels (plan P8). LLR when firing = ln(sensitivity/falsePositive) x grade; when clearly not firing = ln((1-sensitivity)/(1-falsePositive)) x (0.35 + 0.65 x fakeDifficulty). It fires only if p <= alpha AND effect >= minEffect (practical significance, so big samples do not flag trivial differences). affinity = [rotation, laundering, fabricated, other]. class: 'profile' = departs from what is normal, which an honest change can explain and a verified Context Passport can cover; 'conduct' = behaviour a change of business does not explain. A case needs at least one conduct signal. categoryNorm = needs a known category. level = merchant means it cannot be computed for a single QR or payment stream. derivedFrom = built from those detectors, so it is shrunk when they fire and never counts as an independent family. conductWith = this profile signal counts as conduct when one of those detectors also fires.

A1.name: Ticket sizes vs category norm
A1.test: One-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov vs the category's log-normal ticket shape, allowing the merchant's median to sit between one third and 1.8× of the category's; effect = KS distance D.

A4.name: Round-number heaping
A4.test: Beta-binomial upper tail vs category round-amount rate; effect = excess share

A5.name: Deposit / bonus-tier amounts
A5.test: Beta-binomial upper tail vs category rate of betting bonus-tier amounts; effect = excess share

B6.name: Payers from outside the service area
B6.test: Beta-binomial upper tail of payers outside home + neighbouring states vs category rate; effect = excess share

B7.name: Heavy repeat payers
B7.test: Beta-binomial upper tail: share of sales from payers paying >= 8 times in a week vs category rate

B8.name: Repeat deposit-like payers
B8.test: Category-free. Beta-binomial upper tail: share of sales that are ₹100-multiple payments of ₹200+ from payers making >= 4 of them within 14 days, vs 5%

B9.name: Independent purchaser verification
B9.test: Exact binomial lower tail of confirmations vs 80% for genuine merchants; effect = shortfall

B10.name: Distant regulars
B10.test: Category-free. Beta-binomial upper tail: share of sales from out-of-area payers who pay >= 4 times within 14 days, vs 4%

C2.name: Sales outside category trading hours
C2.test: Beta-binomial upper tail of off-hours sales vs category rate; effect = excess share

C5.name: Pre-match funding
C5.test: Permutation test: in-window share on match days vs randomly chosen days (2,000 draws); effect = rate ratio. A profile signal on its own (shops are busy on match nights too); conduct when distant payers (B6) fire with it

C6.name: Rapid rising top-ups
C6.test: Category-free. Beta-binomial upper tail: share of sales inside a same-payer run of 3+ rising payments of ₹200+ within 2 hours, vs 1%

D7.name: Refunds without an original sale
D7.test: Beta-binomial upper tail of orphan refunds vs 2% norm; effect = excess share

D9.name: Refunds paid to someone other than the payer
D9.test: Beta-binomial upper tail vs 5% norm, excluding refunds to the payer's own other accounts; effect = excess share

D10.name: Payments without an order
D10.test: Exact binomial upper tail of unmatched payments vs 5%; effect = excess share

E1.name: Payment link shared with other merchants
E1.test: Deterministic: number of other merchants with links on the same third-party host

E3.name: Continuity with a dormant peer
E3.test: Hypergeometric test of payer overlap with the peer; effect = continuity score (needs a lifecycle hand-off)

F2.name: Account opened as a similar one went quiet
F2.test: Deterministic: account < 45 days old and started within 7 days of a dormant peer's last sale

F5.name: Settlement beneficiary changes
F5.test: Poisson upper tail of beneficiary changes vs category rate per year; needs >= 2 changes or a beneficiary shared with a peer

F7.name: Orders not delivered / reused tracking
F7.test: Exact binomial lower tail of delivered share vs 90%; reused tracking counts as undelivered; effect = shortfall

F8.name: Settlements missing from bank credits
F8.test: Exact binomial upper tail of unmatched settlements vs 2%; effect = excess share

G2.name: Catalogue does not fit the category
G2.test: Exact binomial upper tail of off-category or reused-image items vs 5%; effect = excess share

G6.name: Payment link on an undeclared site
G6.test: Deterministic: link embedded on an undeclared host (marketplaces are UNKNOWN; a known betting host also triggers override R-01)

H1.name: Volume above seasonal expectation
H1.test: Log-normal weekly volume model with festival calendar offsets; Stouffer z over the last 4 weeks; effect = actual / expected

H2.name: Recent change in behaviour
H2.test: Bayesian online changepoint: P(change in last 4 weeks); CUSUM with h set for one false alarm per merchant-year

H3.name: Joint off-profile cluster
H3.test: Beta-binomial upper tail of sales with >= 2 off-profile traits vs what those traits' own rates predict if independent. It measures only the co-occurrence, not the traits again.

I2.name: Onward payouts to many accounts
I2.test: Poisson upper tail of distinct payout beneficiaries vs category norm; effect = ratio

I3.name: Money swept out soon after settlement
I3.test: Exact binomial upper tail of settlements followed by an onward payout within 24 h vs 10%; effect = excess share

K1.name: Declared profile far from category norm
K1.test: Chi-square on standardised gaps between the declared profile and the category norm (catchment, hours width, ticket ceiling, round share)
